task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
within-team variation in role coverage across lineups
separability of role coverage from talent and roster counts
talent control in lineup-level influence estimates
play-by-play-derived possession records (initiator, play type, points)
methodological_questions: Can role coverage be operationalized from play-by-play without using the outcome being explained?
Does role coverage vary within team-season enough to be estimated apart from team and season effects?
Is role coverage separable from talent proxies and from the number of players filling each role?
Does talent control adequately absorb confounding when role coverage is correlated with roster quality?
What reliability and sample-size constraints apply at the lineup and team-season level?
evidence_establishes: retrieve_history returned zero records (n_results = 0), so no earlier study from this project is available for this question, its role definitions, or its talent-control approach.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether lineup role coverage has been tested before, and with what outcome.
Whether any role-coverage measure is reliable, or whether talent control behaves, in this data.
Any effect direction, magnitude, or null result for this question.
own_inferences: The question as posed is not operational: 'organizer', 'shaper' and 'terminal' need explicit, pre-specified definitions from the play-type fields before any test is possible.
Role labels built from initiator and play type in the same play-by-play that produces points risk being partly defined by the outcome.
Within-team variation in role coverage is plausible given rotations, but its amount is unknown until measured.
Talent proxies (for example box-score or on-off measures) are likely correlated with role coverage, so 'talent control behaves' is a testable claim only with a held-out talent measure.
With 90 team-seasons, power for team-level effects is limited; lineup-level models with many correlated possessions per lineup give false precision unless clustered.
uncertainties: The unit count of 90 team-seasons does not clearly match the listed seasons (three full regular seasons would give 90 team-seasons; playoffs and the 2025-26 season add further units); the exact unit definition is unclear.

Data version: the 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) and playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21) are complete as of the 2026-07-13 question date, so they can be used; a partial version must not be mixed in.
The mapping from play-type records to organizer, shaper and terminal roles is not specified in the task.
Reliability of role-coverage measures across seasons is unknown.
No glossary or data-catalog check was run for field-level definitions.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval returned no records, so the decision rests on the task statement and data description alone. The absence of prior work means the question cannot be assumed answered or ruled out, which leaves the decision to the design and risk assessment rather than to any earlier result.

blocking_constraints.text: Role labels derived from the same play-by-play as points risk being defined partly by the outcome; roles must be fixed from pre-specified rules and checked against outcome-independent features.
Role coverage is likely correlated with roster talent and minutes; separating it from talent requires a held-out talent measure that is not itself built from the outcome.
Only about 90 team-seasons are available, so team-level power for detecting a role-coverage effect is limited even though lineup-level possessions are numerous.
Lineup-level role coverage may be unstable across games and seasons, which attenuates estimates unless reliability is measured first.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved (n_results = 0). Whether this question has been answered elsewhere cannot be determined from this setting.

risks.text: Organizer, shaper and terminal labels built from initiator and play type in the same records that produce points may encode the outcome, inflating apparent influence.
Lineups with high role coverage may be high-talent lineups; talent control using outcome-derived or same-game talent measures would be biased.
90 team-seasons limits power for team-level estimates, and the design must avoid treating many possessions as independent.
Role coverage per lineup may have low split-half reliability, attenuating effects and making within-team variation look like noise.
Many lineup-by-role combinations will have few possessions, so coverage categories may be sparse for the rarer roles.
If a role is rare in most lineups, its coverage effect will be estimated from a small share of possessions.
Testing three roles, several coverage definitions and several talent controls invites selection of the best-looking specification.
Without a placebo role or placebo window, a coverage effect cannot be distinguished from generic lineup quality.
Automated play-type classification errors would misassign roles at unknown rates.
Rule and style changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 may shift the meaning of roles over time.
Role coverage must be at least one per lineup by definition in some formulations, so a coverage floor may mechanically produce results.

design.estimand: Within-team, within-season association between lineup role coverage (at least one organizer, shaper, terminal) and lineup-level possession outcomes, conditional on a held-out talent measure, with the coverage effect separated from roster counts.
design.unit: Lineup-stint within team-season, aggregated to lineup-by-team-season for the main test; possessions are the measured quantity, not the independent unit.
design.sample: Complete regular seasons and playoffs only: 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 regular and playoffs, 2025-26 regular (complete from 2026-04-13) and 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21). Exclude any partial pre-completion data. Target the 90 team-seasons, and confirm the unit count before analysis.
design.power: Compute power by simulation before analysis using the observed lineup-stint distribution and team-season clustering; if power for the minimum effect of interest is below 0.8, report the test as exploratory.
design.controls: Talent measured from prior-season or out-of-sample player metrics, not from the same game or season's outcome; team-season and game fixed effects; roster counts of each role as covariates; minutes-weighted lineup exposure; cluster standard errors by team-season.
design.falsification: A placebo role not in the definition set, a placebo time window (for example the first 10 minutes of a game before rotations settle), and a shuffled-role baseline; the coverage effect must exceed both to count as support.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one primary coverage definition and one talent control; treat others as secondary with Holm correction across roles and definitions.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the primary coverage coefficient is positive with a pre-registered 95% CI excluding zero after talent control, survives the placebo role and placebo window, and holds in at least two of the season blocks; rejected if the CI is adequately powered and excludes meaningful effects; otherwise uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for the listed seasons, using only complete regular-season and playoff data as of 2026-07-13; record the data pull date and version hash.
